category_title: Low-attaining students lacking knowledge of mathematical representations like arrays
scenario_title: Calculating products in a playing card multiplication game
minimal_context: Riley is playing a multiplication game using playing cards to generate random numbers and needs to calculate nine multiplied by eight.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: You drew a nine and an eight from the playing cards. Please calculate nine multiplied by eight.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: This is good because it was something different and we get to use playing cards and do the maths questions. Let me try to figure out nine times eight...

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Why don't you use an array to help you calculate it?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I don't know what an array is.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: I will show you what it looks like. Now you try drawing an array of nine by eight to find the answer.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Spends most of the time for the game drawing the array) Okay, I drew an array of nine by eight. The answer is 70.

TUTOR: I will show you what it looks like. Now you try drawing an array of nine by eight to find the answer.

STUDENT: (Spends most of the time for the game drawing the array) Okay, I drew an array of nine by eight. The answer is 70.
